links.outcome: Readability of AI responses on DBS for Parkinson's disease (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Flesch Reading Ease)
links.effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level ranged 14.44 (Gemini) to 18.94 (Copilot); Gunning Fog 17.9 to 22.06; SMOG 16.54 to 19.67; all Flesch Reading Ease scores low, highest 30.91 (Gemini).
links.quote: The Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level scores ranged from 14.44 (Gemini) to 18.94 (Copilot), Gunning Fog Index scores varied between 17.9 (Gemini) and 22.06 (Copilot), SMOG Index scores ranged from 16.54 (Gemini) to 19.67 (Copilot), and all Flesch Reading Ease scores were low, with Gemini showing the highest score of 30.91.

links.outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated responses relative to appropriate user reading level
links.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade levels of 14.44 to 18.94 and all low Flesch Reading Ease scores (max 30.91), indicating complex readability across all chatbots.

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with CNS guideline recommendations on STN/GPi DBS
links.effect: Concordance was 42.9% ChatGPT 4o and 28.6% each for Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini; over-conclusive responses 42.8-57.1%; insufficient 14.3-28.6%.
links.quote: ChatGPT 4o showcased 42.9% concordance, with non-concordant responses classified as 14.3% insufficient and 42.8% over-conclusive.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy (concordance with clinical guidelines) and readability of four commercial LLMs responding to questions about deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease without testing specific organizational deployment safeguards.
